text:
Marathon Petroleum rebounded 2.9% today, recovering most of the ground lost over the prior three trading days. The move follows news that Saudi Arabia and Iran's leadership met to de-escalate tensions, which eased some of the geopolitical risk premium that had spiked oil prices to six-month highs earlier in the week. With crude still holding around $108 per barrel and U.S. refineries running at 93.4% capacity—near full stretch—the company benefits from both elevated oil prices and robust operational demand.

The stock's volatile week reflects the underlying uncertainty: Middle East tensions drove Brent crude above $116, then the prospect of diplomatic talks triggered a pullback. Refiners like Marathon are caught between two offsetting forces—higher crude boosts their feedstock costs but can also widen refining margins when they can pass those costs downstream. At current capacity utilization and oil price levels, the math still favors them, which likely explains today's bounce.
